subject: FinBank evals: post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finbank.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2027 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: FinBank evals: post-call recap & next steps

Alex / Megan — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call:  

Summary:
- Objective: Run customer-specific quality evals on Redwood to validate model fit for transaction categorization + customer support summarization.
- Dataset: FinBank will provide ~10k annotated examples (see attached CSV stub). Expected columns: id, prompt, expected_response, metadata.
- Success criteria: precision/recall for category mapping >= 90% on core categories; summarization measured by embedding-similarity (cosine >= 0.88) and human spot-check on a 200 sample set.

Proposed models to test (start here):
- redwood/gpt-3.8-optimized — balanced latency and quality for short prompts
- redwood/longform-quantized-1 — lower-cost option for long docs (will use 4-bit quant)
- redwood/embedding-ada-2 — for embedding-based similarity scoring

Links:
- Benchmark dashboard: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/finbank-RBW-3421
- Prompt set & rubric (view-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1FinBankEvalAssets

Dataset format (CSV):
- Required columns: id, prompt, expected_response, label
- Optional metadata: source_system, language, confidence
- For summarization evals include: source_text, reference_summary, length_bucket

Scoring guidance:
- Classification: exact match / normalized string match + F1; thresholding and confusion matrix will be reported
- Summarization: embedding similarity (cosine) + ROUGE-L as a tie-breaker; human spot checks for non-numeric quality regressions

Operational ask / next steps:
1) Can you confirm dataset upload (SFTP or shared Drive) and an internal point-of-contact for access?
2) Please confirm NDA/contract path — procurement was on the call, cc'd if we should loop in formal DocuSign.
3) If OK, we'll provision an eval project in your Redwood tenant and run an initial 1k-sample sanity run (estimate: ~2 hours, cost estimate: ~$120). Full 10k run estimate and timeline in attached MA recommendations PDF.

Attachments: finbank-eval-dataset.csv (stub), ma-recommendations.pdf

Thanks — I’ll coordinate provisioning after you confirm upload method.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

- We can share the dataset via our secure SFTP (I will send credentials to Neha).
- Security: we need to confirm that the eval runs can be scoped to a dedicated project and that logs/data are not retained beyond the eval window (we're ok with short-term storage for scoring only). Can you confirm retention controls and do you have SOC 2 evidence we can share with procurement?
- NDA/contract: procurement@finbank.com should receive a templated SOW/NDA. Megan — can you own that?

Also, for the initial 1k run, can you include the exact command/API example we can run (or that you will run) so we can reproduce locally if needed?

Appreciate it — Alex

Alex — great, thanks for the quick reply. Answers below and next actions.

Security / compliance:
- We will create a scoped eval project under your tenant with explicit retention set to 7 days post-run (can be reduced to 0 days if you prefer; we will not persist raw inputs beyond scoring unless you request).
- SOC 2 Type II report and additional artifacts: attaching the SOC2 cover letter link here and I can route the full report to procurement via our security team (we use encrypted transfer).

API / reproducibility:
- Below is a minimal example (pseudo-curl) we will use for the 1k sanity run — Dylan will provision the API key and a temporary service account for your SFTP ingestion job.

  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/evals/run 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <EVAL_KEY>" 
    -F "project_id=finbank-RBW-3421" 
    -F "model=redwood/gpt-3.8-optimized" 
    -F "dataset=@finbank-eval-dataset.csv" 
    -F "score_config=@score-config.json"

- Output: results.json with classification metrics, confusion matrix, and sample-level verdicts.

Next actions (owners):
- Alex / FinBank: share SFTP credentials or Drive link (owner: Alex).
- Procurement: confirm NDA path (owner: procurement@finbank.com).
- Redwood (Dylan / Neha): provision tenant eval project, API key, and run 1k sanity test (owner: Dylan).

I’ve attached a short README (redwood-eval-setup.md) with the dataset schema and scoring defaults. If procurement needs the SOC2 PDF, let me know and I’ll route it via secure transfer.

Thanks — I’ll circle back when Dylan confirms provisioning.

— Marissa
